senses: to fertilize, apply manure to (the soil)
la:verb:laeto.html:
laeto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
id.
,
to make joyful, to delight, cheer, gladden.
Lit. (ante- and post-class.): oculos specie laetavisti optabili, Liv. Andron. ap. : te ut triplici laetarem bono, Att. ib.: frontem alicujus serena venustate,.—
In partic., of the soil, to fertilize, render fertile, manure (postclass.): in laetandis arboribus,: loca sterilia,.

la:verb:laetor.html:
laetor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. [lit. pass. of laeto], to rejoice, feel joy, be joyful or glad

at any thing (syn. gaudeo); constr. with abl., with in, de, ex, or super and abl., with neutr. acc., with acc. and inf., poet. with gen.

With abl.: ut quisquam amator nuptiis laetetur,: et laetari bonis rebus et dolere contrariis,: sua re gesta,: laetor tum praesenti, tum sperata tua dignitate,: laetabitur cor meum quasi a vino,: juvenis specie,.—
With in and abl.: laetaris tu in omnium gemitu,: in hoc est laetatus, quod,because that,: ad laetandum in laetitia gentis tuae,: in Domino,; 84, 7 et saep.—
With de and abl.: de communi salute,: de labore suo,.—
With ex and abl.: Vaccenses ex perfidia laetati,. —(ε) With super (late Lat.): super hederā,; .—(ζ) With neutr. acc.: illud mihi laetandum video, quod,because that,; but rarely with acc. of direct object: laetandum magis quam dolendum casum tuum,: hos erat Aeacides voltu laetatus honores,.—(η) With acc. and inf. (freq. in Cic.): istuc tibi ex sententia tua obtigisse laetor,; : quae perfecta esse gaudeo, judices, vehementerque laetor,: quem esse natum ... haec civitas laetabitur,: utrumque laetor, et sine dolore corporis te fuisse et animo valuisse,; cf.: nec vero Alciden me sum laetatus euntem accepisse,.—(θ) With gen., in connection with memini: nec veterum memini laetorve malorum,.—
Transf., of inanim. subjects, to delight, rejoice, be joyful: omne vitis genus naturaliter laetatur tepore potius, quam frigore,is fonder of warmth than of cold,: frumenta omnia maxime laetantur patenti campo,delight in,: laetatur mons Sion,. 12.— Hence, laetans, antis, P. a., rejoicing, joyful, glad: eos nunc laetantis faciam adventu meo,: nubit Oppianico continuo Sassia laetanti jam animo,—Poet., of inanim. things: loca,delightful, cheerful, agreeable,.—* Adv.: laetanter, with joy, joyfully, .

la:verb:laedo.html:
laedo, si, sum, 3, v. a.
perh. for lavido, root lu-; cf.: luo, solvo, and Germ. los-
,
to hurt by striking, wound, injure, damage (syn.: saucio, vulnero).
Lit.: lora laedunt bracchia,: lembus ille mihi laedit latus,: tua laesuro subtrahe colla,: frondes laedit hiems,: teneros laedunt prima juga juvencos,; cf.: thymum laeditur imbribus,: aliquem vulnere,: quid me dente captas laedere?: ferro retunso Semina,: salsā laedit rubigine ferrum,: servum aliqua parte corporis, Gai .—Poet.: collum,i. e. to hang one's self,: laesus nube dies,i. e. darkened,.—
Trop., to trouble, annoy, vex, injure, offend, afflict, grieve, hurt: dicto, facto,: injuste neminem laesit,: non minus nos stultitia illius sublevat, quam laedit improbitas,: aliquem perjurio suo,to attack,: Pisonem,to rail at,: nulli os,to offend no one to his face,: tua me infortunia laedunt,: tristi laedere versu scurram,: te a me ludibrio laesum iri, Cic. Fil. ap. : quae laedunt oculum, demere,; .—Absol.: quia laesit prior,: nec laedere nec violari,.—
Esp.
Of pledged faith, one's word, agreement, etc., to break, violate, betray: fidem,; : cur tibi junior laesa praeniteat fide,: laesi testatur foederis aras,: laesae vulnera pacis,.—
Of reputation, to harm, injure: famam alicujus gravi opprobrio,.—
Freq. of an offended divinity: quo numine laeso,; : tu magnorum numen laesura deorum,: ego laedor,: Veneris numina,; : superos,.—
Of circumstances: res laesae,disaster, misfortune,.—Esp., in the phrase laedere majestatem, to commit treason (late Lat., v. also majestas): laesae majestatis arcessere maritum,: laesae crimina majestatis,; ; so, laedere majestatem populi Romani,.

la:noun:laena.html:
laena, ae, f., = χλαίνη,
a lined upper garment, a cloak, mantle: laena vestimenti genus habitu duplicis. Quidam appellatam existimant Tusce, quidam Graece, quam χλανίδα dicunt, Paul. ex Müll. Usually worn by the flamens over the toga, ; . Also by persons of distinction,-Verg. l. l.; ; ; ; ; v. Dict. of Antiq.

Laenas, ātis,

la:adj:laetus.html:
laetus, a, um, adj.
Sanscr. root prī-, to cheer; prētis, joy, love; cf. Gr. πραΰς, πρᾷος; Germ. Friede, Freude; cf. also Latin gentile name, Plaetorius
,
joyful, cheerful, glad, gay, joyous, rejoicing, pleased, delighted, full of joy.
Lit., constr. absol., with de, the gen., the inf., or acc. and inf.
Absol.: laeti atque erecti,: alacres laetique,: vultus,: dies laetissimi,.—In neutr. plur. as subst.: litterae tuae partim laeta partim tristia continent,.—
With de: laetus est de amica,.—
With gen.: laetus animi et ingenii,; : laborum,: irae,.—
With inf.: laetus uterque Spectari superis,.—(ε) With acc. and inf.: laetus sum, fratri obtigisse quod volt,: laeta est abs te (donum) datum esse,.—
Transf.
Doing a thing with joy, cheerful, ready, willing: senatus supplementum etiam laetus decreverat,: descendere regno,: fatebere laetus nec surdum esse, etc.,.—
Delighting or taking pleasure in a thing; with abl. or inf.
With abl.: et laetum equino sanguine Concanum,: laetus stridore catenae,: plantaribus horti,.—
With inf.: et ferro vivere laetum Vulgus,.—
Pleased, satisfied with any thing; delighting in; with abl.: classis Romana haudquaquam laeta praedā rediit,: contentus modicis, meoque laetus,.—With gen.: laeta laborum,: laetissimus viae,indulging to the full,.—
Pleasing, pleasant, grateful: omnia erant facta hoc biduo laetiora,: laetique nuntii vulgabantur,: vitium laetissimi fructus,: virtus haud laeta tyranno,: militibus id nomen,.—
Favorable, propitious, prosperous: venti,: sors,: bellum,; : saecula,: exta,: cujus (proelii) initium ambiguum, finis laetior,.—
Fortunate, auspicious, lucky: prodigium,: augurium,: laeta et congruentia exta,: omina,.—
Joyous in appearance, delightful, pleasing, beautiful: vite quid potest esse cum fructu laetius, tum aspectu pulchrius?: segetes,: lupae fulvo nutricis tegmine,: ferarum exuviis,: indoles,: colles frondibus laeti,.—
In partic., in econom. lang., fertile, rich, of soil: ager,: laeta Clitumni pascua,.—Of cattle, fat: glande sues laeti redeunt,.—
Abundant, copious: laeta magis pressis manabunt flumina mammis,; : lucus laetissimus umbrae,.—Of style, etc., rich, copious, agreeable: nitidum quoddam genus est verborum et laetum,.—Of the author: (Homerus) laetus ac pressus,.—
Pleasant, agreeable: dicendi genus tenue laetioribus numeris corrumpere,.—In neutr. sing., adverbially: laetumque rubet,with joy, with pleasure,.— Hence, adv.: laetē, joyfully, gladly, cheerfully.
Lit. (class.): auctorem senatus exstinctum laete atque insolenter tulit,: laete an severe dicere,.—Comp., : neque refert cujusquam Punicas Romanasve acies laetius extuleris,more eagerly,: aliquid ausi laetius aut licentius,.—Sup.: laetissime gaudere,.—
Transf., fruitfully, abundantly, luxuriantly: seges laete virens,.—Comp.: truncus laetius frondet,more fruitfully, more luxuriantly,; cf. .—
Lightly, not severely, without seriousness: si quis putet nos laetius fecisse quam orationis severitas exigat,.

la:noun:laetus.html:
laetus, i, m., in late Lat.,
a foreign bondman who received a piece of land to cultivate, for which he paid tribute to his master, a serf, ; .—Hence,
laeta, ōrum, n., the land so cultivated, Cod. Th. 7, 20, 10.—
laetĭcus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a laetus: laeticae terrae, Cod. Th. 13, 11, 9.

la:noun:laetitia.html:
laetĭtĭa, ae, f.
id.
,
joy, esp. unrestrained joyfulness, gladness, pleasure, delight (cf.: gaudium, hilaritas).
Lit.: laetitia opinio recens boni praesentis, in quo efferri rectum esse videatur,: laetitia dicitur exsultatio quaedam animi gaudio efferventior eventu rerum expetitarum,: judicium plenum laetitiae,: percipere laetitiam ex re,: prae laetitia lacrumae prosuliunt mihi,: ut mea laetitia laetus promiscam siet,: totus in laetitiam effusus,wholly dissolved in pleasure,: diem perpetuum in laetitia degere,to spend joyfully,: ne me in laetitiam frustra conicias,: laetitiae dator,i. e. Bacchus,: efferri laetitiā,to be transported with joy,: exsultare,: perfrui,: afficere aliquem,: comitia me laetitiā extulerunt,have rejoiced me exceedingly,: laetitiam capere oculis,to enjoy,: dare alicui,to give delight to,: et altera traditur circensis turbae non minus similis veri laetitia,another outbreak of joy,: ut hanc laetitiam nec opinanti primus ei obicerem domi,this cause of joy,; cf.: offerre laetitiam alicui,.—Esp. of success in love, ; .—Plur.: quaero quoi ter trinas triplicis tribus demeritas artibus Dem laetitias,: incessi omnibus laetitiis laetus, Poët. ap. .—
Transf., pleasing appearance, beauty, grace: membrorum,.—Luxuriance, fertility, of plants: trunci,: pabuli,plenty, abundance,.—Of a fruitful soil: loci,.—Of speech, sweetness, grace: laetitia et pulcritudo orationis,.

la:adj:laevus.html:
laevus, a, um, adj.
cf. Gr. λαιός
,
left, on the left side (mostly poet.; syn.: sinister, scaevus).
Lit.: ut idem nunc sit laevus; et e laevo sit mutua dexter, (325): manus,: ab laeva manu,: habeo equidem hercle oculum. Py. At laevom dico, : latus,: auris : pes,: umerus,: Pontus,lying to the left,: iter,: habena,: amnis,the left bank,: laevā in parte mamillae,. —
Subst.
laeva, ae, f.
(Sc. manus.) The left hand: opsecro te hanc per dexteram, perque hanc sororem laevam,: Ilionea petit dextrā, laevāque Serestum,; ; 7, 188: cognovi clipeum laevae gestamina nostrae,; ; 8, 321: hinc factum est ut usus anulorum exemtus dexterae, in laevam relegaretur,; so, dextera laevaque,; .—
(Sc. pars.) The left side: laevam cuncta cohors remis ventisque petivit,: laevam pete,go to the left,.—Esp. freq. adv.: laevā, on the left side, on the left: dextrā montibus, laevā Tiberi amne saeptus,on the left,: dextrā laevāque duo maria claudunt,: so, a laevā: Diana facem jacit a laeva, Enn. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 55 Vahl.); .—So, ad laevam, in laevam, to the left, on the left: ante, et pone; ad laevam, et ad dexteram,: si in laevam detorserit,.—
In neutr.: laevum, on the left (poet.): intonuit laevum,; : laevum extendere comas,: in laevum, adverbially, to the left: fleximus in laevum cursus,: dixit in laevum conversus, (Jahn, in laevam).— Plur.: laeva, ōrum, n., places lying on the left: laeva tenent Thetis et Melite,: Thracen et laeva Propontidos intrat,.—
Trop.
Awkward, stupid, foolish, silly: si mens non laeva fuisset,; : o ego laevus, Qui purgor bilem sub verni temporis horam,.—
Of ill omen, unfavorable, inconvenient; unfortunate, unlucky, bad, pernicious: Sirius laevo contristat lumine caelum,: peccatum fateor, cum te sic tempore laevo Interpellarim,: teque nec laevus vetat ire picus,: laevo monitu pueros producit avaros,: omen,: ignis,i. e. a pestilence,; ; Rupert; so, numina laeva (opp. dextra or propitia),unfavorable gods, hostile deities, Jahn and Forbig. ad loc.: impia Cappadocum tellus et numine laevo Visa tibi,; ; ; .—
In the language of augurs, fortunate, lucky, propitious (because the Romans, by turning their faces to the south, had the eastern signs on their left hand; v. sinister): laeva prospera existimantur, quoniam laevā parte mundi ortus est,; cf. : omina,: tonitru dedit omina laevo Juppiter,; cf. ; (I. B. 2 supra).—Hence, adv.: laevē, awkwardly, wrongly (poet.), .

la:other:Laelius.html:
Laelĭus, a,
name of a Roman gens.— So esp.,
C. Lælius, a friend of Scipio Africanus: in quo Laeliu' clamores, σοφὸς ille, solebat Edere, Lucil. ap. ; cf.: nec dubitare illum (C. Laelium) in omni sermone appellare sapientem,; ; cf. ; . Cicero's treatise on Friendship is named after him.—
D. Lælius, a writer of moderate abilities, Lucil. ap. .—
Another D. Lælius, perh. a son of the preceding, an adherent of Pompey, .—In fem.: Laelĭa, ae, daughter of C. Lælius, and mother-in-law of L. Crassus, celebrated for her intellectual culiure, .—Another Lælia, a Vestal, .—Hence, Laelĭā-nus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Lælius, Lælian: naves, i. e. of Pompey's commander, D. Lælius, .
